artifacts.claim_authorized: Local relation-objective smoke only: a balanced logistic classifier over source/target node-pair features distinguishes observed typed ZE2020 x sector candidate edges from controlled non-edges, but only as a diagnostic. It uses typed hard negatives by default (cross_ze_same_sector keeps the same sector and changes ZE; intra_ze_sector keeps the same ZE and changes sector). Local smoke over 2021-2025 showed relation_logit full_control ROC-AUC ~0.762 / AP ~0.783 against typed_hard negatives, while easy random negatives were much easier (ROC-AUC ~0.951 / AP ~0.931). Added artifact controls show pair_history (~0.894 AP) and target_popularity (~0.884 AP) beat relation_logit in the core all-pair full_control typed_hard scenario. In stricter unseen_pair mode, relation_logit beats recurrence/popularity controls (AP ~0.579 vs ~0.195 target_popularity / ~0.172 pair_history), but temporal_shuffle and random_edge_targets still block promotion. Lag-1 feature mode predicts relation labels at t using node features from t-1; it preserves signal above controls (full_control AP ~0.550) but remains tied with temporal_shuffle and far below random_edge_targets. Every output row uses claim_status=dynamic_relation_learner_smoke_exploratory_not_recommendation.
artifacts.claim_forbidden: Treating this as a validated dynamic graph model, a validated GNN, or authorization for HPC. Treating the local relation learner as evidence of causal economic influence or automatic sector recommendation. Treating edge magnitude as learned economic intensity -- edge_sign_only exactly matched full_control in the local smoke. Treating the task as solved -- random_edge_targets improved the metric, temporal/sector shuffles did not hurt, all-pair recurrence/popularity controls beat the learned classifier, and lag-1 features still do not pass shuffle/random-target controls, which blocks promotion and points to source-target/type distribution artifacts.
